name: Zitadel
tagline: An API-first identity platform with a hosted option
description: An identity platform written in Go: single sign-on over OpenID Connect and SAML, passkeys and multi-factor sign-in, and organisations as a built-in concept, so one install can serve several companies or your own customers. Everything in the console is also available through its API.
licenseNote: AGPL-3.0 since version 3 in 2025; earlier versions were Apache-2.0. The same code runs the company's own cloud service.
backing: Zitadel, a venture-backed company founded in Switzerland, funded by its cloud service and support contracts

maturity.rationale: In production use and actively developed, with an audit trail built into its design. Younger than Keycloak, it changed licence and narrowed its supported databases in 2025, and still moves at a pace that rewards reading release notes.

selfHosting.summary: A single binary or container in front of PostgreSQL. A test instance is quick; production needs TLS and a correct external domain setting, database backups, and outgoing mail for verification and recovery.

managedHosting.label: Zitadel Cloud
managedHosting.note: Run by the developers, with a free tier

strengths: A hosted service from the developers, so you can leave Entra without running a login server
Organisations are built in: useful for agencies, groups of companies, or software with customer logins
Passkeys and multi-factor sign-in are built in
Every change is recorded in an audit trail and reachable through the API
weaknesses: Younger, with fewer ready-made app integrations and guides than Keycloak
LDAP support is for signing in only: there is no continuous sync from a directory
No login proxy or LDAP interface for software that lacks single sign-on
Does not push accounts out to other apps; it only accepts SCIM from them

featureNotes.scim: Accepts SCIM from other systems; does not send it
